archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A short, mobile passer whose best plays come when he leaves the structure: his scrambles and checkdowns produce more than his drop-back passing, which runs on accurate short throws and pays a steep sack tax.

report.headline: Accurate, mobile, sack-prone, and now hurt and listed behind Cousins.
report.take:
Murray in Minnesota has been a caretaker more than a centerpiece. The Vikings are 5-1 in his starts, but that record belongs to the league's best defense (team.defEpa ranks 1st), not to an offense that ranks 30th in EPA. His own passing sits at -0.044 EPA per dropback, 31st of 55 and a touch below the league average of -0.027. He has kept games on schedule, but he hasn't won them. The numbers show a quarterback whose accuracy is real, with a 2.06 CPOE (17th) on throws that are mostly short, and whose rushing is the best part of his game: 27.8 rush yards a game ranks 7th, and his 16 scrambles have averaged 0.593 EPA with 8 first downs.

The drag on the season is sacks and wasted throws. His 8.9% sack rate ranks 40th, and he turns 38.5% of pressures into sacks. That is no Minnesota quirk. Across his career he has never been good at avoiding sacks, and last year's 50% pressure-to-sack rate ranked 56th of 62. His time to throw rose to 2.95 seconds this year, up 0.27 from last, which fits a passer holding the ball to make something happen. The scrambles partly repay that, but not on third down, where his plays have totaled -14.3 EPA. Screens and throws behind the line have been worse, at -12.9 EPA in total.

The splits also show what the offense does well with him. Under center and on play-action looks he has added +5.9 EPA, against -21.1 from shotgun. In other words, he is better when the structure is built for him than when he is asked to drive the ball from spread looks. Hockenson has been his most efficient target by far at 0.486 EPA per target. Addison, who is out, has been a net negative at -0.128. Before the injury Murray was trending up: over his last three games he was at +0.054 EPA per dropback and 7.45 adjusted net yards per dropback. Most of that came from one sharp game at New Orleans, though, and his bad-throw rate climbed in Weeks 7 and 8.

The bigger issue now is the job itself. He is Out with a hamstring strain and listed as QB2, with Kirk Cousins starting Weeks 10 and 11. The dossier doesn't say whether that is an injury placeholder or a demotion. For the rest of the season, Murray's value depends first on getting healthy and then on getting the job back. When he plays, expect a low-volume, run-supported passer with a fantasy floor built on his legs.

strengths.title: Scrambles that actually pay
strengths.body: His 16 scrambles have produced 0.593 EPA each and half of them moved the chains. That is the main return on his long time to throw: when the pocket breaks down, he creates rather than just absorbing a sack. The rushing floor has held up across his whole career, and it is the most bankable part of his game.

strengths.title: Accurate in the short game
strengths.body: On throws of 0-9 air yards he completes 80.3% with a 9.8 CPOE, and his overall CPOE ranks 17th, well above the league average. This lines up with his best career seasons, when CPOE ran positive. The accuracy is real, even if the aggressiveness isn't there.

strengths.title: Better in structure than spread
strengths.body: Under center he has averaged +0.15 EPA a play, against -0.163 from shotgun. When the play-action and under-center menu sets up his throws, he is a positive passer. That tells the staff how to use him if he returns. With only 39 under-center plays, it is a lean worth trusting but not a law.

concerns.title: Sacks are a career trait
concerns.body: His 8.9% sack rate ranks 40th, and he converts 38.5% of pressures into sacks. His career shows the same thing every year, peaking at a 50% pressure-to-sack rate in 2025. The scrambles recover some of the cost, but the sacks are part of his style, not bad luck, and they will keep capping his efficiency.

concerns.title: Third downs and screens bleed points
concerns.body: His third-down plays total -14.3 EPA, with a 36.2% conversion rate facing an average of 8.1 yards to go. Throws behind the line total -12.9 EPA. Together they wipe out everything his downfield passing earned. Some of this is play-calling and long yardage, but the sacks on third down are his.

concerns.title: Injured and listed as backup
concerns.body: He is Out with a hamstring strain and sits at QB2 on the depth chart, while Cousins started the last two games. A hamstring also threatens the scrambling that props up his value. Even when healthy, his path back to the field isn't guaranteed.

trend.note: He went from -9.5 passing EPA at Tampa to +6.7 at New Orleans, then slipped back below zero against Indianapolis and Detroit, with bad-throw rates of 20.8% and 28.6% in those two games. His rushing kept climbing, which lifted his last-three numbers above his season line.

nextGame.headline: Ruled out against a soft Falcons defense he can't exploit
nextGame.body:
Murray is Out for Week 12, so this matchup belongs to whoever starts, most likely Cousins. Had he played, it would have suited him. Atlanta allows 19 PPR points a game to quarterbacks (27th) and ranks 31st in explosive runs allowed, which is exactly where his scrambles do damage. Its 21st-ranked sack rate would also have eased his biggest flaw, though its 6th-ranked hit rate means pressure still arrives.

On the Atlanta side, linebacker Divine Deablo (78% of snaps) is out, which thins the second level that chases quarterback runs. On Minnesota's side, Jordan Addison (92% of snaps) is out after thumb surgery. That matters less for Murray's efficiency, since Addison has been a negative target for him, than for the offense's depth at receiver. Minnesota is a 7-point favorite with a 42.5 total in a dome, which points to a run-and-defend script either way.

keyMatchups.title: Scrambles vs leaky run defense
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta ranks 31st in explosive rush rate allowed. That is the matchup his legs would have targeted. It is worth remembering for a rematch or a late-season return.

keyMatchups.title: Generous to quarterbacks overall
keyMatchups.body: The Falcons allow 19 PPR points a game to the position, 27th in the league, and rank 18th in pass EPA allowed. That is a mid-to-soft spot for any Minnesota starter.

keyMatchups.title: Addison out, Hockenson central
keyMatchups.body: With Addison out, the passing game leans on Hockenson, who has been Murray's most efficient target. Atlanta has held top tight ends roughly to their norm.

nextGame.watch: Whether Minnesota names Murray the starter again once his hamstring clears, or keeps Cousins in the job.

restOfSeason.body:
If Murray gets back on the field, expect what he has been: a low-volume passer in a defense-first, slightly run-leaning offense. He would throw about 25-30 times, complete a high share of short passes, and take too many sacks. His legs would supply much of his fantasy value. I'd project 165-215 passing yards and 22-38 rushing yards a game. His late-stretch bump came mostly from one game, so expect his passing EPA to settle near league average rather than stay above it. His zero fumbles lost will probably regress as well.

The hamstring is the real swing factor. A strained hamstring is the injury most likely to dull the scrambles that keep his game afloat. He also has to win back a job Cousins currently holds. Until both are settled, any projection for him is conditional on him playing at all.

confidence.note: Six starts, a hamstring strain and a QB2 listing make his role uncertain.
